finding.title: Request email is interpolated into a SQL statement
finding.evidence: The request-derived email is inserted into SQL syntax before sqlite3 executes it.
finding.remediation: Bind the email as a sqlite3 parameter instead of formatting it into the SQL text.

cases.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+import sqlite3
+from flask import Blueprint, jsonify, request
+
+bp = Blueprint("customers", __name__)
+
+@bp.get("/customers/search")
+def search_customers():
+    email = request.args.get("email", "")
+    db = sqlite3.connect("customers.sqlite")
+    query = f"SELECT id, email, status FROM customers WHERE email = '{email}'"
+    rows = db.execute(query).fetchall()
+    return jsonify(rows)
human_review_rubric: Confirm true_positive because request data is part of the SQL text, not a separately bound value.
Recommend sqlite3 parameter binding; manual quote escaping is not an equivalent primary fix.
Propose a regression test where SQL metacharacters remain literal email data and do not broaden returned rows.
cases.rationale: The patch exposes a complete source-to-sink flow: an HTTP query value changes SQL syntax through an f-string.
cases.expected_safe_behavior: Use a constant SQL string with a ? placeholder and pass (email,) as the separate parameter tuple.
cases.known_limitations: Synthetic Flask example adapted from documented SQL-injection patterns; it does not reproduce the Metabase advisory implementation.

finding.title: Request email is passed to a database query

finding.title: Upload path is interpreted by a command shell
finding.evidence: The form-controlled path is concatenated into a command string executed with shell=True.
finding.remediation: Pass a fixed executable and separate argv entries without a shell, and constrain the file path to server-managed uploads.

cases.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+import subprocess
+from flask import Blueprint, jsonify, request
+
+bp = Blueprint("uploads", __name__)
+
+@bp.post("/uploads/inspect")
+def inspect_upload():
+    path = request.form["path"]
+    command = "file --brief " + path
+    completed = subprocess.run(
+        command,
+        shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
+    )
+    return jsonify(kind=completed.stdout.strip())
human_review_rubric: Confirm true_positive based on shell=True and concatenated request data.
Recommend a fixed argv list and address option injection or server-side path lookup; quoting the string is weaker.
A regression test should show metacharacters cannot start an additional process and must not claim execution unless run.
cases.rationale: Both shell interpretation and an untrusted value in the command text are explicit.
cases.expected_safe_behavior: Resolve a server-managed upload path, then run ["/usr/bin/file", "--brief", "--", path] with shell disabled.
cases.known_limitations: Synthetic endpoint isolates command injection and does not model upload authorization or file-content scanning.

finding.title: Upload identifier reaches a subprocess invocation
finding.evidence: A numeric identifier selects a server-side filename; subprocess receives a fixed argv list, --, and shell=False.
finding.remediation: No command-injection change is supported by this patch; preserve the argument boundary.

cases.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+from flask import Blueprint, abort, jsonify, request
+
+bp = Blueprint("uploads", __name__)
+UPLOADS = Path("/srv/app/uploads").resolve()
+
+@bp.post("/uploads/inspect")
+def inspect_upload():
+    upload_id = request.form["upload_id"]
+    if not upload_id.isdecimal():
+        abort(400)
+    path = UPLOADS / f"{upload_id}.bin"
+    completed = subprocess.run(
+        ["/usr/bin/file", "--brief", "--", str(path)],
+        shell=False, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
+    )
+    return jsonify(kind=completed.stdout.strip())
human_review_rubric: Return false_positive for command injection because shell=False and the explicit argv list prevent shell parsing.
Recognize the decimal identifier, fixed directory, fixed suffix, and -- option terminator as relevant controls.
Do not invent shell expansion or claim unrelated upload authorization is present.
cases.rationale: The input cannot become shell syntax because no shell parses it, and it cannot become an option after the explicit -- separator.
cases.expected_safe_behavior: Keep the executable fixed, use separate arguments, retain --, and keep the identifier constrained.
cases.known_limitations: The verdict is limited to command injection; file authorization and resource exhaustion need separate review.

source_refs.title: OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization

finding.title: Authenticated user can request invoices by global ID without object authorization
finding.evidence: The route authenticates the caller but retrieves by invoice_id alone and returns the object.
finding.remediation: Scope the lookup to an organization or policy the current user may access and use a non-disclosing not-found response.

cases.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+from flask import Blueprint, abort, jsonify
+from flask_login import current_user, login_required
+
+from services.billing.models import Invoice
+
+bp = Blueprint("invoices", __name__)
+
+@bp.get("/invoices/<int:invoice_id>")
+@login_required
+def get_invoice(invoice_id: int):
+    invoice = Invoice.query.get(invoice_id)
+    if invoice is None:
+        abort(404)
+    return jsonify(invoice.to_dict())
+
+# current_user is authenticated but is not used in the lookup.
human_review_rubric: Confirm true_positive because login_required establishes identity but does not authorize access to this invoice ID.
Recommend policy-aware query scoping rather than only checking that the ID is well formed or unguessable.
A cross-tenant test should deny another user’s invoice while preserving access to an allowed invoice.
cases.rationale: Authentication is explicit, yet no owner, tenant, sharing, or policy condition participates in the object lookup.
cases.expected_safe_behavior: Authorize every requested invoice against current_user, preferably by scoping the database query to an allowed tenant or policy.
cases.known_limitations: The synthetic model omits administrator and sharing rules; a real fix must encode the application policy rather than assume ownership.
